title: Ann Arbor Home Energy Rebates 2026: A2ZERO City Rebates and DTE
desc: Ann Arbor home energy rebates in 2026: the city's A2ZERO rebates (heat pump $4,000, insulation, battery, panel) plus DTE rebates, free help and a state program.
h1: Home Energy Rebates in Ann Arbor
lead: Ann Arbor is the one Michigan city we cover that pays its own home energy rebates. The city's A2ZERO program pays up to $4,000 for a cold climate heat pump ($5,500 for lower incomes), and also covers insulation, a heat pump water heater, an electrical panel and a battery. DTE Energy rebates sit on top. We read both on October 6, 2026.
cards_heading: What is open for Ann Arbor homes in 2026
cards_intro: Each card names the fact we keep on file. The city's amounts come from its A2ZERO rebates page, and the DTE amounts come from DTE's own pages. The city says rebates cannot be more than 90% of the cost of the measure or project.

cards.title: A2ZERO cold climate heat pump
cards.note: Unit must be listed on the NEEP cold climate list with a 15.2+ SEER2 and 8+ HSPF2 rating. Dual-fuel systems are not eligible. Contractor install, a Manual J sizing report and an AHRI certificate are required.

cards.title: A2ZERO heat pump water heater
cards.note: Needs a UEF rating of 2.0 or higher and contractor installation.

cards.title: A2ZERO insulation and air sealing
cards.note: Air sealing is $500 ($1,000) and needs a blower door test before and after with at least 20% less leakage. Combined bonuses are listed on the city page.

cards.title: A2ZERO electrical panel and battery
cards.note: Lower-income amounts are $2,000 and $3,500. A battery must be at least 13 kWh.

cards.title: DTE heat pump
cards.note: Only for electric customers replacing electric heating.

cards.title: DTE insulation
cards.note: For DTE gas customers, with a 500 square foot attic.

cards.title: DTE Wi-Fi thermostat
cards.note: One per home. Apply by December 31, 2026.

cards.title: State home energy rebates (MiHER)
cards.note: The state paused new income-qualified applications in five districts. The page does not say which district Ann Arbor is in, so look up your county on the state's map.

cards.title: Federal 25C and 25D tax credits
cards.note: The federal home energy credits ended for work finished after December 31, 2025. A quote that counts on them is out of date.

sections: How Ann Arbor heats and lives

The Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) counts 54,399 housing units in Ann Arbor. More than half of households rent (54.5%), and 45.5% own. Utility gas heats 70.7% of homes and electricity heats 26.1%, a bigger electric share than in Detroit, Grand Rapids or Lansing. Only 41.6% of homes are detached houses. Another 12.3% are attached homes and 8.8% are in buildings of two to four units.
Older homes, but newer than Detroit's

63.4% of Ann Arbor homes were built before 1980 and 14.8% before 1940. About 15.9% date from 2000 or later. That is a younger mix than most Michigan cities, so insulation upgrades pay off most in the older neighborhoods, and the city's air sealing rebate fits homes where a blower door test shows real leaks.
Renters can use the city program

The city says you can apply if you own or rent a home in Ann Arbor, as long as the work is a retrofit and you are at least 18. That is unusual. Most utility rebates go only to the account holder for a single-family home. A renter should still get the landlord's written approval before any work on the building.

The higher amounts are for households at or below 120% of area median income. The city page lists $116,200 for one person and $166,000 for four. The city says it set aside about $1.9 million from its Community Climate Action Millage, with about half for income-qualified households. Verifying income takes up to 10 business days, so start that step first.
A note about the EV rebates
The city also pays EV rebates, but its page said on August 17, 2026 that all of them were reserved, with a waiting list. We cover home energy here, not EVs.
claim_heading: What to do in Ann Arbor
claim_steps: Read the city's technical rules for the measure you want, such as the NEEP heat pump list.
If you may be income-qualified, verify your income with the city's rebate team first.
Reserve the rebate funds before you buy. The city says approval takes up to 10 business days.
Finish the project within 90 days of approval and send the full application.
Expect the check in 6 to 8 weeks, and apply separately to DTE for its rebates.
faq: Does Ann Arbor have its own heat pump rebate?
Yes. The city's A2ZERO program pays $4,000 for a cold climate heat pump, or $5,500 for lower-income households.
Can I get the city rebate and DTE's rebate together?

The city's page does not say they are barred from combining. DTE's heat pump rebate is only for electric customers replacing electric heating, so many gas homes will claim only the city's. Ask both programs before you sign.

No. It ended for work finished after December 31, 2025.
